source: Deadlands: The Weird West core rules (player extract)

edges.name: ACE
edges.text: Some folks are just born to fly—be it dirigibles, experimental ornithopters, or one of those newfangled gliders from the Collegium. They ignore two points of penalties to any Boating, Driving, or Piloting roll, and may spend Bennies to Soak damage for any vehicle they control or command, using the appropriate Boating, Driving, or Piloting skill instead of Vigor. Each success and raise negates a Wound.

edges.name: ACROBAT
edges.text: The Acrobat gets one free reroll on Athletics totals that involve balance, tumbling, or grappling. It doesn’t affect rolls to interrupt actions, climb, swim, or throw.

edges.name: AGENCY PROMOTION
edges.text: This Edge reflects a promotion by the Agency for your hero’s devotion, loyalty, and effectiveness. The first time it’s taken they become a Grade 1 Agent. This grants them a slight pay raise, the ability to spend higher Favors, and a light armored vest (or corset) if they choose (see page 127). The second time they take this Edge they becomes a Grade 2 Agent. They get another pay raise, the ability to call for greater Favors, and a mnemomizer. A player character can take this Edge one final time at Heroic Rank. This makes them a Grade 3 Agent and allows them to ask for 4-point Favors.

edges.name: AGENT
edges.text: The shadowy Agency is responsible for rooting out sedition, treason, espionage, corruption, and illegal acts that might plunge the country into another Civil War. Agents are a secretive lot who don’t share information outside their ranks if they can avoid it—not even with the local law. They’re expected to conceal their credentials except under extreme and desperate circumstances. Read the top secret details on page 65.
edges.requirements: Novice, Smarts d8+, Fighting d6+, Occult d6+, Shooting d6+

edges.name: ALCHEMY
edges.text: (Mad Scientist), Weird Science d8+ Weird scientists can already make potions, elixirs, tinctures, and the like depending on the Trappings of their powers. They can use them on others, but can’t “give” them to others unless they craft the item with the Artificer Edge (see page 49). The Alchemy Edge is a bit of a cheat, allowing a character to create up to three potions or elixirs, investing a single Power Point in each. Creating the potions takes 30 minutes and $5 worth of various reagents each, and always includes at least a pinch of ghost rock. No Weird Science roll is made—creation is automatically successful, and creates any mix of the potions listed below. These can be given away freely and last for 24 hours. The scientist doesn’t get the Power Points back until they’re used, discarded, or expire. Drinking one potion is an action.  SNAKE OIL: The recipient makes a natural healing roll. Success heals one Wound and a raise heals two.  FOCUSING ELIXIR: Add +1 to any one Trait’s rolls (alchemist’s choice when created) for three rounds.  PEPTONIC: The recipient makes a Vigor roll. Success removes one level of Fatigue, and a raise removes two.

edges.name: ALERTNESS
edges.text: Not much gets by this hero. They’re very observant and perceptive, and add +2 to their Notice rolls to hear, see, or otherwise sense the world around them.

edges.name: AMBIDEXTROUS
edges.text: Your warrior is as deft with their left hand as the right. They ignore the Off-Hand penalty (see page 160). If holding a weapon in each hand, Ambi dextrous characters may stack Parry bonuses (if any) from both weapons.

edges.name: ARCANE BACKGROUND
edges.text: Certain characters can call upon supernatural power. In the Weird West, there are eight types, detailed on the listed pages.  BLESSED: Page 68.  CHI MASTER: Page 70.  HARROWED: Page 72.  HUCKSTER: Page 83.  MAD SCIENTIST: Page 87.  SHAMANS: Page 92.  VOODOOISTS: Page 97.  WITCHES: Page 99.  NOTE: Arcane Background (Black Magic /Magic /Miracles) is the generic Edge used by some nonplayer characters who fall outside those paths available to player characters. Those with Black Magic or Magic use Spellcasting as their arcane skill, while those with Miracles use Faith. Both have however many Power Points and abilities the Marshal feels is appropriate to their background (nonplayer characters don’t advance like player characters). Critical Failure on an arcane skill roll causes a level of Fatigue and all currently active powers terminate instantly. Marshals have more rules on page 247 for Black Magic in Deadlands.

edges.name: ARCANE RESISTANCE
edges.text: Magic and the supernatural hold little sway with this maverick. Whether by nature, heritage, or training they’re particularly resistant to magic, weird science, and other supernatural energies. Enemy arcane abilities targeting the hero suffer a −2 penalty and magical damage is reduced by 2 as well. If a hostile power fails to affect the hero due to this penalty, it still activates and consumes Power Points (and may still affect other targets). This includes magical bonuses granted to weapons, such as the smite power or the damage bonus of magical weapons.

edges.name: ARCANE RESISTANCE (IMP)
edges.text: As above, but the penalty to the arcane skill roll and damage are increased to 4.

edges.name: ARISTOCRAT
edges.text: Some folks ride into town with dust on their boots and nary a penny to their name. Others show up in a fine coat with bank notes to some Eastern fortune or foreign title. Your cowpoke may or may not be flush with cash, but they walk the walk and talk the talk of the upper crust—be it railroad barons, foreign dignitaries, or highfalutin’ Society types with their pinky fingers raised. The character was born into privilege or came into it later in life. They may or may not have money (the Rich or Filthy Rich Edge), but still walk in the elite social circles of their locale. Aristocrats add +2 to Persuasion when Networking (see page 228) with the local elite, captains of industry, nobles, or other aristocrats. They also add +2 to Common Knowledge rolls made to know the etiquette of the upper class, recognize family trees or heraldry, or recall gossip concerning others of their station.

edges.name: ARTIFICER
edges.text: (Any) Some folks don’t just cast spells—they etch them into iron, lace them into charms, or whisper ‘em into moonshine. Heroes with this Edge can craft Arcane Devices and hand ‘em off to allies like chips at a high-stakes poker game. Artificers can create Arcane Devices and give them to their allies. See page 170.

edges.name: ASSASSIN
edges.text: In the Weird West, quiet killers ain’t just myths whispered about in saloons. Whether working for the Agency, the Reckoners, or a personal vendetta, assassins know how to kill without a trace. They add +2 to damage rolls when their foe is Vulnerable or they have The Drop.
edges.requirements: Novice, Agility d8+, Fighting d6+, Stealth d8+

edges.name: ATTRACTIVE
edges.text: In a world full of grimaces and grit, a friendly smile and a pretty face can go a long way. Whether it’s batting lashes or flashing a charming grin, this Dapper Dan knows how to turn heads and smooth talk their way through trouble—especially if the target’s partial to their look. The character adds +1 to Performance and Persuasion rolls if the target is attracted to their general type (gender, sex, species, etc.).

edges.name: BEAST BOND
edges.text: Some folks in the Weird West have a way with critters. Whether it’s a faithful hound, prairie falcon, or mighty stallion, these bonds run deeper than blood. These characters may spend their own Bennies for any animals under their control, including mounts, pets, familiars, and so on.

edges.name: BEAST MASTER
edges.text: Not all men and women get along with the beasts of the land, but some have a spark that makes animals sticks to them through thick and thin with tooth, claw, or wing. Animals take to your hero quickly and easily. Critters won’t attack them unless threatened or attacked first. The Beast Master’s “animal magnetism” is so great she’s also attracted a loyal animal companion of Size 0 or smaller, subject to the GM’s approval. The beast is an Extra and doesn’t Advance in Rank or abilities. If a pet is dismissed or killed, the hero gains a replacement in 1d4 days. More Powerful Companions: Beast Master may be taken more than once. Choose one of the effects below each time it’s chosen: • Gain an additional pet. • Increase one of the pet’s Traits one die type (only one Trait per pet). • Increase the maximum Size pet you may have by +1, to a maximum of 3. • Make one pet a Wild Card. (The hero must be of Heroic Rank).

edges.name: BEEN TO THE CROSSROADS
edges.text: ground (Voodooist), Faith d8+ This hero nearly died at some point but came back. They’ve seen the crossroads between worlds, and the spirits hear their call better than most. This Edge may only be taken after character creation. The character must have been Incapacitated due to an effect that could cause death (not getting enough sleep doesn’t count, amigo). Once the voodooist is no longer Incapacitated, either because they’re healed or come b a c k Harrowed, they get a free reroll on Faith rolls.

edges.name: BEHOLD A PALE HORSE...
edges.text: The Lone Ranger had Silver, Zorro had Toronado, and your caballero’s steed is no less impressive. Whether it’s a new stallion or the same faithful pony your hero’s had since they were young, there’s something special about this horse. It has character. The faithful beast uses the statistics for a war horse (see page 319) but gains the Fearless special ability and the Danger Sense Edge. What’s more, the horse is a Wild Card, and starts each session with its own two Bennies. If the trusty steed dies, your hombre can start training another, a process that usually takes a few weeks of game time (GM’s call).

edges.name: BERSERK
edges.text: When this fighter takes a lick, something snaps. They go wild-eyed and roaring, hitting like a freight train and damn near impossible to stop. But with rage like that comes recklessness, and more than one ally’s taken a swing meant for the enemy. Immediately after suffering a Wound or a Shaken result (from physical damage only), your hero must make a Smarts roll or go Berserk. They can voluntarily fail this check if desired. Going Berserk has the following effects:  FURY: The character’s Strength increases a die type and every melee attack must be a Wild Attack (see page 165). They cannot use any skills that require wit or concentration (GM’s call). They may scream out threats and use Intimidation, for example.  ENRAGED: Adrenaline and rage fuel the berserker’s muscles, adding +2 to Toughness. They ignore one level of Wound penalties (this stacks with any other abilities that reduce Wound penalties).  RECKLESS ABANDON: Anytime a berserker rolls a Critical Failure on a Fighting check, they hit a random target within range of their attack (not the intended target), friend or foe. If there are no applicable targets, the blow simply misses, smashes nearby objects, etc. After five consecutive rounds of berserk fury, the hero takes a level of Fatigue. At ten rounds, they take another level of Fatigue and the rage ends. They may also choose to end their rage at any time by making a Smarts −2 roll (as a free action; possibly avoiding Fatigue if this ends the rage before it’s incurred!). Start the count anew if they go berserk again, even in the same battle.

edges.name: BLOCK
edges.text: Close scrapes has taught your scrappy hero how to turn blades, ducks fists, and come out grinnin’. Their Parry increases by +1 and any Gang Up bonus against them is reduced by one.

edges.name: BLOCK (IMP)
edges.text: The hero’s Parry bonus is now +2 and the Gang Up bonus against them is reduced by 2.

edges.name: BOLSTER
edges.text: Nothing lifts a cowpoke’s spirit like watchin’ a loudmouth get taken down a peg. When this character successfully Tests a foe—maybe with a well-placed insult or some quick shootin’ sass—they can also snap an ally out of being Distracted or Vulnerable (page 155).

edges.name: BORN IN THE SADDLE
edges.text: Some folks spend so much time on horseback, it’s as if they were born in the saddle and live entirely in it. There’s no place they’d rather be than on the back of a trusty steed. Heroes with the Born in the Saddle Edge get a free reroll on Riding rolls. They also know how to get the most out of their trusty steeds in an emergency. This increases their horse’s Pace by 2 and their running die one step.

edges.name: BRAVE
edges.text: Terrors walk the West—shadows that shriek, ghosts that whisper, and beasts best left undescribed. This hero’s seen things that would drive most to prayer or panic, but they steel themselves against it. They’ve stared into the maw of madness and didn’t blink. These valiant explorers add +2 to Fear checks and subtract 2 from Fear Table results (see 217).

edges.name: BRAWLER
edges.text: Your cowpoke hits like a freight train and soaks up hurt like a cast-iron bathtub. Brawlers increase their Toughness by 1 and roll Strength +d4 when hitting with their fists or feet. If they already have a damage die from Claws (page 310), the Martial Artist Edge, etc., increase the damage die type by one instead. The Brawler Edge doesn’t make the character’s fists Natural Weapons (page 159).

edges.name: BRAWNY
edges.text: Big as a barn and twice as solid, this gal could lift a steer and throw it at ya! They’re the kind of bruiser who can carry more gear than a pack mule and still have room for a Gatling pistol. Your bruiser is very large or very fit. Their Size increases by +1 (and therefore Toughness by 1) and they treat Strength as one die type higher when determining Encumbrance (page 116) and Minimum Strength to use armor, weapons, and equipment without a penalty (page 114). Brawny can’t increase a character’s Size above +3.

edges.name: BRUISER
edges.text: Now the brute is a real bone-breaker. The fighter increases their Toughness an additional +1, and the damage caused with their fists or claws another die type.

edges.name: BRUTE
edges.text: Not everyone is built for finesse. Some bruisers train their bodies to punch through brick walls instead of jump over ‘em. This one’s all power, no polish. They can hurl a stick of dynamite further than most folks can spit and hold their ground when the ground starts shakin’. Brutes focus on core strength and fitness over coordination and flexibility. They treat Athletics as linked to Strength instead of Agility for purposes of Advancement. The character may also resist Athletics Tests with Strength if they choose. Finally, Brutes increase the Short Range of any thrown item by +1. Double that for the adjusted Medium Range, and double again for Long Range. If a thrown item’s Range is 3/6/12, for example, a Brute’s Range is 4/8/16.

edges.name: BURROW
edges.text: The Harrowed gains the ability to burrow through raw earth, per the power (page 177). Although this makes them a very efficient traveler underground—the earth seems almost eager to get out of their way—they always finish such a trip covered with soil, slime, millipedes, centipedes, and such subterranean accouterments. The deader can burrow into loose earth and move through it at half normal Pace (they cannot run). They cannot normally be attacked while burrowing, and can attempt to surprise opponents who didn’t see them coming by making an opposed Stealth vs. Notice roll. If successful, the burrower adds +2 to their attack and damage rolls that round, or +4 with a raise (they have The Drop).

edges.name: CALCULATING
edges.text: This big brain can often calculate their moves. When their Action Card is a Five or less, they ignore up to 2 points of penalties on one action that turn, which can include Multi-Action, cover, Range, and even Wound penalties.

edges.name: CARD SHARP
edges.text: Your hero has a knack for odds, wagers, and when to call a bluff. They never feel more at home than when they’re shuffling cards, tossing dice, or calculating the chances of some wager. Your character gets one free reroll when making a Gambling roll. That includes hucksters who Deal with the Devil (see page 84)!

edges.name: CAT EYES
edges.text: The deader’s eyes glow slightly in the dark, enhancing light and negating all Dim and Dark penalties.

edges.name: CAT EYES (IMP)
edges.text: The hero can see perfectly in the dark and ignores all penalties for lighting.

edges.name: CELESTIAL KUNG FU
edges.text: Kung Fu, Fighting d10+ More options become available to a martial artist as they master the mystical and physical aspects of their art. A hero with this Edge gains an additional style from Superior Kung Fu and may assume two styles at once using either or both options as they see fit. They may change one or both as a free action at the start of their turn.

edges.name: CHAMPION
edges.text: There are those who walk the dusty trails of the West not just with iron on their hips, but with holy fire in their hearts. Whether it’s the work of the Almighty or some darker force, Champions are chosen to stand against unnatural evils—or deliver fiery destruction if they’ve thrown in with the Devil. Champions fight the forces of darkness (or good), adding +2 damage when attacking supernaturally evil (or good if they’re evil) creatures. The bonus applies to area effect damage, ranged attacks, powers, etc. The GM must decide which foes this bonus applies to, but generally it’s any evil (or good!) creature born of magic or with any supernatural abilities.

edges.name: CHANNELING
edges.text: (Any) Some spell-slingers or weird scientists learn to let the energy flow clean and easy, like a stream fed by mountain snow. When they get a raise on an arcane skill roll—or when using a contraption—they ease the burden, reducin’ the Power Point cost by 1 (even down to 0).

edges.name: CHARISMATIC
edges.text: Your hero is likable for some reason. They may be trustworthy or kind, or might just exude confidence and goodwill. You get one free reroll on Persuasion rolls.

edges.name: CHARNEL BREATH
edges.text: Charnel Breath is the ability to dredge up all the worst stench of decay in a Harrowed’s body, supernaturally fester it even further, and blow it out all over an unsuspecting target within arm’s reach. The corrosive gas produces watery eyes and violent retching. To do so, they breathe a cloud of noxious fumes in a Medium Blast Template adjacent to their position. Everyone within must make a Vigor roll at −2 or suffer Fatigue. This effect can only cause Incapacitation, not death. Beings that don’t breathe are immune to Charnel Breath. A Harrowed can wretch up these foul vapors only after eating something and waiting at least an hour—it has to “simmer” in their wretched innards for a while.

edges.name: CHI
edges.text: Your hero’s martial arts training goes beyond the norm and into the realm of the mystical. At the start of each combat encounter, they gain a “Chi Point” that can be spent to: • Reroll one of their failed attacks (even a Critical Failure). • Make an enemy discard an attack against them, then reroll it from scratch. • Add +d6 damage to a successful Fighting attack made with their hands, feet, claws, or other Natural Weapons (this may Ace). Unspent Chi is lost at the end of the combat encounter.

edges.name: CHILL O' THE GRAVE
edges.text: The Harrowed radiates the icy chill of death in a Large Blast Template centered on themself. This costs a Benny and takes an action. Living beings in the template who aren’t protected by cold weather gear or the like are automatically Vulnerable.

edges.name: CLAWS
edges.text: The hero gains sharp claws that cause Str+d6 damage in combat. The Harrowed can extend or retract the claws as a free action.

edges.name: COMBAT ACROBAT
edges.text: The tumbler leaps quickly about so that attacks against them are made at −1 as long as they’re aware of the attack, can reasonably move about, and aren’t suffering any Encumbrance or Minimum Strength penalties.

edges.name: COMBAT REFLEXES
edges.text: Your warrior bounces back faster than a jackrabbit on a hot skillet. They add +2 to their rolls when attempting to recover from being Shaken or Stunned.

edges.name: COMMAND
edges.text: A real leader can keep a posse calm even when they’re facing down a chupacabra or a horde of walkin’ dead. Extras in Command Range add +1 to their Spirit rolls when attempting to recover from being Shaken and Vigor when attempting to recover from being Stunned.

edges.name: COMMAND PRESENCE
edges.text: This honcho’s presence hits like a thunderclap on the plains. A booming voice, effective commands, natural charisma, or simple training results in a much more effective combat element. A hero with this Edge has a Command Range of 10″ (20 yards).

edges.name: COMMON BOND
edges.text: In the Weird West, folks who stand alone don’t stand long. This hero shares their luck with the posse, passing good fortune along with a word of hope, a steady hand, or maybe just a sharp bark to snap someone out of their fear. A character with this Edge may freely give their Bennies to any other character they can communicate with. The player should explain what form this takes, from a quick shout of encouragement to a welcome pat on the back.

edges.name: CONCENTRATION
edges.text: (Any) Some of those with hoodoo can quiet the world like still water. Through grit, prayer, or sheer focus, these arcane types hold their magic longer than most. The base Duration of any non-Instant power is doubled. This includes maintaining powers as well.

edges.name: CONNECTIONS
edges.text: Whether they know a ghost rock tycoon, a high-up in the Explorer’s Society, or someone deep in the Black River payroll, this hero’s got ties. Once per session, they can call in a favor—from shady deals to timely reinforcements—as long as they can get word to their people. Connections may be taken more than once, selecting a new faction or contact each time. Once per session, and assuming they can get in touch with them, the heroine can call on their friends for a favor. The favor depends on the nature of the contact (GM’s call), but might include a loan, gear, a few allied fighters, transportation, information, or even a professional with critical skills the party doesn’t have, like a hacker or scholar.

edges.name: COUNTERATTACK
edges.text: You miss this brawler, you might just lose teeth. Once per round (if not Shaken or Stunned), the character receives a Free Attack (page 156) against one failed Fighting attack against them. The counterattack takes place immediately (before other hits against the hero on the same Action Card, if any).

edges.name: DAMNED
edges.text: Old gunslingers don’t die, they just… Okay, they do die. Usually in messy and embarrassing ways. But if your grizzled veteran of the Weird West goes down, they’re definitely coming back. Taking this Edge is an insurance policy against having your plans for this old hand ended prematurely. If your hero is killed, they automatically return from the grave as a Harrowed (see page 72 for details). Just how long that takes relies on the Marshal’s whim and the story. It could be near-instant, or it could be after your partners put you in a pine box and read the 23rd Psalm. Once you return as Harrowed, you may trade this Edge for an additional Harrowed Edge.
edges.requirements: Wild Card, Legendary, Spirit d6+, Reputation

edges.name: DANGER SENSE
edges.text: It’s not always the eyes or ears that save a soul in the Weird West—sometimes it’s just a gut feeling, a twitch in the spine, a cold shiver right before all hell breaks loose. This hombre’s got the kind of sixth sense that kicks in right before the lead starts flyin’ or the floor gives way. Your hero can sense when something bad is about to happen. When rolling for Surprise (page 164), they add +2 to their Notice roll to act in the first round. With a raise, they start the encounter on Hold. In other situations not covered by the Surprise rules (a sniper shot, pit trap, poisoned drink, etc.), Danger Sense gives them a Notice roll at −2 (or +2 if a Notice roll is usually allowed) to detect the hazard and take appropriate action. If this was an attack and the hero makes their Notice roll, the foe doesn’t get The Drop against them.

edges.name: DEAD MAN’S HAND
edges.text: Harrowed with this power can continue to control their own severed body parts— usually a hand or an eye—for short periods of time. To use the Edge, the deader slices off their own hand or plucks out an eyeball. The severed body part remains active and under its owner’s mental control up to a Range of one mile. The deader can maintain the Dead Man’s Hand as long as they wish, though they have the One Arm or One Eye Hindrance until the body part is reattached. Severed hands use the Animate Hand profile (see page 321). They can “walk” on their fingers at a Pace of 6 (no running). Eyeballs magically transmit back whatever they see to the owner, and can roll around at a Pace of 6 (no running). Ears can’t move on their own, but if left behind somewhere they relay whatever they “hear” back to their owner. Healing: Severing a body part causes an immediate Wound and any Hindrance associated with it (One Eye for the removal of an eye, One Arm for a hand, Hard of Hearing for an ear, and so on). Sewing the body part back on reattaches it, but it doesn’t actually work until the next time they make a successful natural Healing roll.

edges.name: DEAD RECKONING
edges.text: Dead Reckoning is the ability to sense the direction to any and all corpses—animal, human, or otherwise—within a mile. This shows up almost like radar in the Harrowed’s mind. Bits and bones show up as small “blips” while fresh bodies are larger. Detecting the dead is an action but doesn’t require a Trait roll. And yes, it can absolutely be used to tell if an individual is a walking corpse, though it doesn’t tell them what kind—another Harrowed, vampire, walking dead, etc.

edges.name: DEAD SHOT
edges.text: Shooting d8+ This shootist has a deadly sense of timing. When your Action Card is a Joker, double the total damage of your first successful Athletics (throwing) or Shooting roll this round.

edges.name: DEATH MASK
edges.text: sion d6+ Use of this Edge allows a Harrowed to appear as they did when they still drew breath, negating others’ Unfriendly attitudes and the Harrowed’s innate −2 Persuasion penalty. Death Mask is an action to activate but doesn’t require a Trait roll. Once activated, the Harrowed can keep it up as long as they like. The effect is a minor illusion, so if the Harrowed is Shaken, Stunned, or suffers one or more Wounds, they must make a Spirit roll at −2 to keep the disguise active. Detect arcana automatically sees through this effect, and a successful dispel removes it.

edges.name: DEVIL’S TOUCH
edges.text: A Harrowed with this Edge can disrupt the workings of any mad scientist’s gizmo or Infernal Device with a touch. This is an action and a Spirit roll. If successful, any failure when using the device counts as a Critical Failure. This lasts for three rounds after the device is touched, or five with a raise.

edges.name: DODGE
edges.text: The hero can anticipate attacks or move erratically under fire. Unless the victim of a surprise attack and taken completely unaware, Dodge subtracts 2 from all ranged attacks made against the character. Dodge does not stack with actual cover, however.

edges.name: DODGE (IMP)
edges.text: The hero adds +2 when Evading area effect attacks. See Evasion on page 156.

edges.name: DOUBLE TAP
edges.text: Quick as a blink, and twice as deadly, this shooter can fire two shots in rapid succession without spoiling their aim. Double Tap can only be used with weapons that have a Rate of Fire of 1 and can fire two shots without needing to manually reload. It adds +1 to hit and damage at the cost of one extra bullet. This is per action, so a shooter can Double Tap more than once if they perform a Multi-Action. Double Tap cannot be combined with Rapid Fire, and doesn’t work with Single-Action revolvers. If used with a weapon capable of Three- Round Burst (rare in the Weird West, but possible; see page 115), it adds +2 to Shooting and damage instead of +1 and expends six bullets. DON'T GET 'IM RILED! REQUIREMENTS: Novice The hero with this Edge can be a real curly wolf when they get roughed up. When causing melee damage, they add their Wound levels to the roll. A hero with three Wounds, for instance, adds +3 to their melee damage rolls!

edges.name: DUELIST
edges.text: Your hombre is a deadly gunfighter, and anyone foolish enough to face them at High Noon is likely to end up in the boneyard by sunset. In a duel, this hero receives two extra Hole Cards at the start of the throwdown. Rules for Dueling can be found on page 215.

edges.name: ELAN
edges.text: When things get dicey, some folks flinch. Not this one. They rise up, burning with fire and determination, driven by some deep well of spirit that pushes them to shine brightest when the chips are down. When you spend a Benny to reroll a Trait, add +2 to the total. The bonus applies only when rerolling. It doesn’t apply to damage rolls (since they’re not Trait rolls), nor does it apply to Soak rolls unless you’re using another Benny to reroll the Vigor check.

edges.name: EXPERT
edges.text: affected Trait As the Professional Edge, increasing the Trait and its limit one additional step.

edges.name: EXTRA EFFORT
edges.text: (Gifted), Focus d6+ Some of the Gifted dig deep—real deep— when times are tough and boost their powers. Extra Effort increases a Focus total after it’s rolled by +1 for 1 Power Point, or +2 for 3 Power Points. It may not be used to improve a Critical Failure.

edges.name: EXTRACTION
edges.text: When this dude backs out of a scuffle, they’re slicker than a greased pig. Adjacent attackers usually get a free Fighting attack when a character Withdraws from Melee (see page 165). This can be a very dangerous proposition for most, but not your wily rogue. They ignore the attack of one such foe (player’s choice).

edges.name: FAME
edges.text: This traveler is a known face—maybe from posters, dime novels, or leaving a trail of busted-up bad guys behind in their wake. Whether they’re a singer, shootist, or stage star, folks recognize ‘em and are usually willin’ to help... or challenge ‘em, if they’re feelin’ lucky. They make double the normal fee when performing for pay (see Performance, page 34). They can also use their celebrity to add +1 to Persuasion rolls if a target is friendly and knows who they are (Common Knowledge modified by how likely the individual is to know the celebrity). The downside of Fame is that the individual is often recognized, others frequently want something from them, they may be followed by fans or admirers, or they might be hunted by someone out to prove they’re better!

edges.name: FAMILIAR
edges.text: (Witch), Spellcasting d8+ Your witch has a small (Size −3) creature that serves them. The familiar has the Loyal Hindrance to its mistress but isn’t a slave. It acts like a typical but very smart version of its species and can occasionally be distracted by its own inherent instincts. A cat might interrupt its task to chase a mouse or take a brief nap and will most likely hide during combat. A familiar is a Wild Card with respect to Wounds and rolling a Wild Die with its Trait rolls. It doesn’t get Bennies, but the witch can spend her own on its behalf. The familiar can understand its mistress’s speech and vice-versa (others hear only the creature’s natural sounds). The bond between the familiar and its mistress makes it immune to the beast friend power. If a familiar dies, the witch is automatically Stunned (no matter how far away it is). They can summon another after 13 days, and can change the type if they choose. Familiars do not advance as allies. Instead, a familiar has any one of the advantages below for each of the witch’s Ranks (including Novice) and for every fourth advance the witch gains past Legendary, gaining them as they advance or starting with them if they must replace a fallen pet. Only increasing a Trait or gaining an Edge may be taken more than once.  The witch can transfer Wounds and Fatigue to and from the familiar as a free action.  The witch can increase one of the familiar’s Traits one die type. This may only be taken once per Trait.  Your witch can use the familiar’s senses as if they were their own. This requires concentration and the maximum range for this ability is 10 miles.  The familiar gains an Edge. It must make sense for the familiar’s species and meet the Requirements as usual.  The familiar has 5 Power Points of its own. It cannot cast spells, but the witch can draw on them as if they were their own. They recharge separately and at the same rate as the witch’s.

edges.name: FAMOUS
edges.text: Now your cowgirl is truly famous. They’re widely known and generally admired throughout the West and likely Back East as well. They make 5× the normal fee when performing and add +2 to Persuasion rolls when influencing friendly individuals who know who they are. The price is higher for the truly Famous, too, with more demands on their time, obligations, rivals, scandals, and an inability to operate in crowds without being recognized.

edges.name: FAN THE HAMMER
edges.text: Most folks have trouble enough drawing a bead and hitting a target with a single shot. The supremely skilled shootist with this Edge can play the “six-gun symphony,” firing their pistol faster than chain lightning. A gunslinger who wants to “fan the hammer” holds the trigger of a single-action pistol down while repeatedly slapping the hammer with their other hand. Assuming their six-gun is fully loaded, they may fire up to six shots in a single action. Each shot is a Shooting die at a −4 Shooting penalty, along with the Wild Die if the shooter is a Wild Card. A player character firing all six shots, for example, rolls six Shooting dice and one Wild Die. What you lose in accuracy you (hopefully) make up for by getting lead in the air! Just watch who’s about when you’re fanning the hammer, partner. If your Shooting die comes up 1 or 2, there’s a chance you hit an Innocent Bystander (see page 158).

edges.name: FAST AS DEATH
edges.text: Normally, dead bodies don’t move very fast. But the Harrowed with this Edge can move with supernatural speed when the need arises. This increases Pace by 3 and her running die one step. This stacks with Fleet- Footed and similar abilities!

edges.name: FAST AS LIGHTNING
edges.text: When your hero reaches for their shootin’ irons, folks rarely have time to blink, much less draw down. Some say they’re the fastest gun in the West. Your hero gets a fourth action. This increases the maximum Multi-Action penalty to −6 (which can be reduced by any Edges or abilities that do so, such as Two-Fisted or Two-Gun Kid).

edges.name: FAST HEALER
edges.text: Some folks just bounce back. Could be clean living, a strong constitution, or maybe some deal made under a blood moon. Either way, this one stitches up faster than most and shrugs off hurts that’d lay another soul low. Those with this blessing add +2 to Vigor rolls for natural healing, and check every three days instead of five (see Healing, page 186).

edges.name: FAVORED
edges.text: Background (Voodooist), Faith d8+ This Edge may only be taken once, and signifies a special relationship between a mambo or houngan and a particular loa. It only benefits those who have the aspect of the rada loa or fury of the petro loa spells.

edges.name: FEINT
edges.text: When performing a Test (page 164) with the Fighting skill, you can choose to make the foe resist with Smarts instead of Agility.

edges.name: FERVOR
edges.text: Fiery words, a battle cry, a hymn from an old gospel, or something older still can inspire others to bloody fervor. Extras in range add +1 to their Fighting damage rolls. HOLD THE LINE! REQUIREMENTS: Seasoned, Smarts d8+, Command The line holds—not because it’s safe, but because this leader wills it so. Maybe it’s a marshal with nerves of steel or a tough old sergeant with fire in their gut. Hold the Line strengthens the will of any Extras under the hero’s command, adding +1 to their Toughness.

edges.name: FETISH
edges.text: Background (Shaman), Faith d8+ Fetishes are devices that help a shaman focus when they must contact the spirit world. It might be a stick figure that represents a favored animal, an icon of nature, or a rattle that helps draw the attention of the distant nature spirits. A shaman with a fetish gets one free reroll when they make a Faith roll. Should a fetish be lost or destroyed, the shaman may create a replacement with a one-hour ritual.

edges.name: FILTHY RICH
edges.text: This fortunate individual is very wealthy. They have five times the starting funds for the setting during character creation ($1,250) and, if appropriate, a yearly income after responsibilities of around $10,000. Even wealthier characters may exist, but unless there’s a game effect it probably shouldn’t matter. This should be worked out with the GM and come with many more assets as well as onerous responsibilities.

edges.name: FIRST STRIKE
edges.text: Move into reach of this wrangler and you’ll eat a fist full of knuckles. Once per round, as long as they’re not Shaken or Stunned, the hero gets a free Fighting attack immediately after a foe moves into Reach. (See Free Attacks on page 156).

edges.name: FIRST STRIKE (IMP)
edges.text: As above but the hero may attack up to three foes each turn.

edges.name: FLEET-FOOTED
edges.text: Whether they’re runnin’ from a lynch mob or racing the 4:15 to Yuma, this cowpoke moves like greased lightning. Folks swear they saw ‘em in two places at once—and they’re usually gone before the dust settles. The hero’s Pace is increased by +2 and their running die increases one step (from d6 to d8, for example).

edges.name: FLOCK
edges.text: (Blessed), Persuasion d8+ The greatest prophets and preachers are attended by followers. These men and women have found salvation of one sort or another in the blessed, and devoted their lives to their cause. Flock gives your padre five followers who serve at their side in whatever capacity you choose. They have the stats of Townsfolk (see page 318), though like any other Allies they may Advance (see page 111). They come with nothing but the clothes on their back and a few dollars, but can be armed and outfitted however the blessed sees fit. Members of the Flock who perish are slowly replaced over time (usually by giving a “revival”). The Edge may not be taken more than once until the blessed is Legendary. At that point they may take it as many times as they like (as well as the Followers Edge, if they choose).

edges.name: FOLLOWERS
edges.text: Each time this Edge is chosen, five followers come to fight by the hero’s side. If any are lost, others eventually take their place (how long is up to the GM and the circumstances). Followers must be cared for and generally want a share of whatever loot, treasure, or other rewards the hero acquires. Otherwise, they are completely dedicated to their task. They won’t throw their lives away but are willing to risk them repeatedly in their service. Use the Soldier profile found on page 317 for the followers. A hero may outfit their allies as they see fit. Followers Advance just like player characters (see page 111). Use the Allies rules on page 203 to give them distinctive personalities if desired.

edges.name: FREE RUNNER
edges.text: Your nimble character is very skilled at running, jumping, swinging, scampering up walls, and over obstacles. As long as there are obstacles they can bound on, bounce off, or swing on, they move at full Pace on Difficult Ground when on foot. They also add +2 to Athletics rolls when climbing and in foot Chases on page 205).

edges.name: FRENZY
edges.text: This scrapper swings like a Texas twister. As a limited action, a character with Frenzy may roll a second Fighting die with any one of their Fighting attacks for the turn. The extra die may be allocated to the same or different targets as the player sees fit. Resolve each separately.

edges.name: FRENZY (IMP)
edges.text: As Frenzy but the fighter adds a third Fighting die to their Fighting attack made with Frenzy this turn. Example: Red uses her Colts to pistol whip a walking dead. She has Frenzy (Imp) and decides to attack three times (a Multi-Action at the usual penalty). She rolls her Fighting skill with two extra dice for her first attack, but doesn’t get the extra dice on her second or third Fighting rolls.

edges.name: GADGETEER
edges.text: (Weird Science), Weird Science d6+ Some mad scientists can slap together miracles outta baling wire, ghost rock, and gumption! A Gadgeteer can spend up to three Power Points to “jury rig” a device from any reasonable collection of spare parts. This allows them to activate any power normally available to Mad Scientists of their Rank or lower, with a Power Point cost of 3 or lower. The total cost of an individual power (plus any modifiers) cannot exceed the points spent to create it, nor can the inventor apply Limitations to the gadget. They may attempt to create multiple devices as long as they have the points to do so. Each gadget is created and activated with a Weird Science roll at −2. This takes one entire turn, during which they can do nothing else (they cannot take Multi-Actions that turn). In all other ways, it works as the normal activation of a power. The inventor uses Power Points directly from their pool for the device, but once its initial Duration is finished (it cannot be maintained) it falls apart into its component pieces. Example: Gabe has Arcane Background (Mad Science). He wants to use boost Trait to help Red fight a giant rattlesnake, but only has the burst and blast powers. Fortunately, he’s a Gadgeteer, so Gabe can put boost Trait into an “electrical bio-inducer.” The device can take up to three points worth of powers, so he adds the Hurry modifier and gives Red +2 Pace as well.

edges.name: GALLOWS HUMOR
edges.text: Some people make jokes about the direst situations. They can stare the Grim Reaper himself in the face, just so long as something about him strikes them as funny. It’s a skill that serves anyone well. A character with this Edge may use their Taunt skill instead of Spirit when making a Fear check (and all the usual modifiers apply as normal). If they get a raise, they mock the threat so effectively it acts as +1 Support for all allies making the same Fear check. Just make sure you roll and resolve your Fear check first, partner!

edges.name: GHOST
edges.text: The Harrowed can become incorporeal at will. While ghosted, they’re intangible but still visible, and magical attacks affect them normally. The deader decides if they’re corporeal or incorporeal at the beginning of their turn. This is a free action, but they must remain in that state until they’re next turn. The deader is Distracted as long as they remain in ghost form, but may remain so as long as they wish. If they’re Shaken, Stunned, or Wounded while incorporeal, they must make a Spirit roll or immediately become corporeal.

edges.name: GIANT KILLER
edges.text: The bigger they are, the harder they are to kill. At least for most. Your hero knows how to find the weak points in the most massive of foes. They add +1d6 damage when attacking creatures who are three or more Sizes larger than themselvew (see Size, page 161). A human (Size 0) gets the bonus against a creature of Size 3 or greater.

edges.name: GREAT LUCK
edges.text: The player draws two extra Bennies instead of one at the start of each session.

edges.name: GRIT
edges.text: The Weird West ain’t for the faint of heart, partner. Folks who survive out here have nerves like barbed wire and wills like granite. Grit’s what keeps a soul from breaking when the wind howls and something evil comes crawling outta the dark. Through perseverance and maybe a little insanity, this hardcase reduces penalties to the Fear check by 2. This stacks with Brave.

edges.name: GUTS
edges.text: A hero with this Edge has learned to steel themself against the horrors that stalk the Weird West. They get a free reroll when making Fear checks.

edges.name: HARD TO KILL
edges.text: This adventurer has more lives than a herd of cats. They may ignore their Wound penalties when making Vigor rolls to avoid Bleeding Out (see page 149).

edges.name: HARDER TO KILL
edges.text: Your hero is tougher to kill than a three- headed rat. If killed, roll a die. On an odd result, they’re dead as usual. Even, they’re Incapacitated but somehow escape death. They may be captured, stripped of all their belongings, or mistakenly left for dead, but somehow survive.

edges.name: HARROWED
edges.text: Some folks just don’t know when to die— and a rare few come back after crossing over, dragged outta the grave by things from the depths of the Abyss. They walk the earth again, hollow-eyed and cold as the grave, with death whispering in one ear and life clinging to the other. The price they pay is an eternal battle for their own soul. If you take this Edge, your character has been reborn into unlife and you can read the grisly details on page 248. The Harrowed Edge may only be selected at character creation. To become Harrowed later requires shedding the mortal coil and a whole lot of luck (the Marshal has information on how this might occur), or by taking the Damned Edge at Legendary Rank. Note: Talk it over with your Marshal before you take this Edge, because it sometimes becomes an involuntary Hindrance to everyone else in the posse!

edges.name: HEALER
edges.text: In a land of hexes, hauntings, and horrors, someone who can patch up a bullet wound or pull a soul back from the brink is worth more than their weight in ghost rock. A hero with this Edge adds +2 to all Healing rolls, whether natural or magical in nature.

edges.name: HELL STEED
edges.text: God’s critters don’t take so well to the unholy abominations called the Harrowed. Dogs bark, buzzards circle warily overhead, and horses snort and buck at a would-be rider who stinks of death. But a Hell Steed is a strange kind of horse dredged up from the Hunting Grounds by the Harrowed’s manitou. When summoned (by taking this Edge), it charges out of some Hell bound portal, snorting fire, eyes blazing, and a cloud of brimstone following in its wake. Within a few minutes the beast comes to terms with the mortal realm and becomes a normal horse—though one that’s clearly fierce and powerful. The horse has the usual stats for a War Horse (page 319), is Fearless, and a Wild Card. The beast is loyal and has sinister intelligence that understands its master’s commands (treat its Smarts as human intelligence rather than animal). It’s a strange creature, and serves the human as well as their manitou when the demon has control of the host’s body. If the Hell Steed is ever slain, the Harrowed doesn’t automatically get a replacement! They can take the Edge again to summon a new beast, however. A Harrowed can’t have more than one Hell Steed at once.

edges.name: HELLFIRE
edges.text: Raw, blazing fire blasts straight from the depths of Hell through the Harrowed’s fingertips. This takes an action but may only be used once per turn. The attack uses the Athletics skill and Cone Template, and causes 3d6 to those unfortunate enough to be caught in the template. Hellfire may be evaded.

edges.name: HEXSLINGING
edges.text: Background (Huckster), Shooting d8+ John Henry “Doc” Holliday was a huckster who learned the secrets of “rune magic,” a process the ancient Vikings used to enchant their weapons in days long past. He carved the runes on his favorite six-gun and “hexslinging” was born. Taking a cue from Hoyle, Doc passed those techniques on to his friends in a series of dime novels appropriately called The Adventures of Doc Holliday. Hexslingers who learn Holliday’s secrets gain the ammo whammy power (page 172) and can create their own rune- engraved “hex guns.” This takes four hours per weapon, most of which is spent inscribing the barrel with various runes. The weapon can be any firearm—a pistol is common, but nothing stops a hero from making a hex gun out of a derringer or even a Gatling if they want! Once complete, any hexslinger can use that weapon to cast any of the following powers (assuming they have them) on or with the hex gun without incurring a Multi-Action penalty: ammo whammy, deflection, boost Shooting, and protection. These spells have a Range of Self when cast in this way and can’t use the Additional Recipients modifier if they have it. Activation causes the runes on the weapon to glow subtly, throw sparks, or some similar effect.

edges.name: HIGH ROLLER
edges.text: Go high or go home. Your hero draws an extra card anytime they Deal with the Devil (see page 84).
edges.requirements: Seasoned, Spirit d8+, Arcane Background (Huckster), Spellcasting d6+

edges.name: HOLY/UNHOLY WARRIOR
edges.text: (Miracles), Faith d6+ The faithful are often called on to face the dangers of the Reckoning. To survive such hardships, the forces of good (or evil) grant miracles and the ability to turn their favor into supernatural protection. The chosen may add +1 to the total of a final Soak roll for each Power Point spent, to a maximum of +4.

edges.name: HUMILIATE
edges.text: Some folks draw a six-shooter. Others draw blood with a smirk and a sneer. This character’s wit cuts deep enough to leave a scar, and they get a free reroll on Taunt Tests when twistin’ the verbal knife.

edges.name: IMPLACABLE
edges.text: Deaders are a tough and ornery lot fueled by the infernal power of demons. Eventually, some of ‘em can take a hit that’d drop any normal hombre. A deader with this Edge can take an extra Wound before they’re Incapacitated. This stacks with the Tough as Nails and Tougher than Nails Edges, and their maximum Wound penalties are still limited to −3.

edges.name: IMPROVED CLAWS
edges.text: The Claws now inflict Str+d8 damage, AP 2.

edges.name: IMPROVED COUNTERATTACK
edges.text: This hombre is quicker than a rattler in a dogfight. As above but the hero gets a Free Attack against up to three failed attacks each round.

edges.name: IMPROVED EXTRACTION
edges.text: Up to three foes’ (player’s choice) don’t get attacks when your warrior moves out of melee with them.

edges.name: IMPROVED FAN THE HAMMER
edges.text: Hammer, Shooting d10+ As Fan the Hammer, above, but each shot suffers a −2 Shooting penalty.

edges.name: IMPROVED RAPID FIRE
edges.text: The shooter may now increase their weapon’s Rate of Fire by 1 twice in the same turn (via a Multi-Action). Example: Gabe fires a steam Gatling and has Improved Rapid Fire. The weapon has a Rate of Fire of 3 and Gabe decides to fire it on all three of his allowed actions (see Multi-Actions on page 159). He rolls an extra Shooting die with his first and second attack, raising the weapon’s Rate of Fire to 4 each time. He doesn’t get the bonus on his third attack—the machine gun’s Rate of Fire remains a 3.

edges.name: IMPROVED RAPID RECHARGE
edges.text: The character now regains 20 Power Points per hour spent resting.

edges.name: IMPROVED TRACKIN’ TEETH
edges.text: Teeth As above, except the piece can be tracked up to 100 miles away.

edges.name: IMPROVED TRADEMARK WEAPON
edges.text: As above but the bonuses when using the weapon increase to +2.

edges.name: IMPROVISATIONAL FIGHTER
edges.text: Anything’s a weapon in the right hands. A brawler with this Edge can use a table leg on a head like an artist uses a paintbrush on a canvas. They ignore the usual −2 penalty when wielding improvised weapons. See page 158 for details on Improvised Weapons.

edges.name: INFEST
edges.text: Like many aspects of nature, insects have spiritual counterparts in the Hunting Grounds. Manitous have a knack for controlling creepy-crawlies, and some pass this along to their hosts. A character with this icky ability can control swarms of biting or stinging insects. Infest doesn’t give the Harrowed the ability to actually create bugs or summon them from great distances. They must already be present in the immediate vicinity (Marshal’s call), but the deader’s swarm doesn’t have to be composed of a single species. To summon the swarm, they use an action and spend a Benny to call forth a mass of spiders, roaches, and millipedes into one wriggling, biting, unholy horde. The Harrowed controls the swarm until it dissipates—when destroyed or after about five minutes. See Swarm (page 320) for the critters’ statistics and Special Abilities.

edges.name: INSPIRE
edges.text: Exceptional leaders inspire those around them to great feats of valor and determination. As a limited action, the hero may roll their Battle skill to Support one type of Trait roll, and apply it to all allied Extras in Command Range. A leader could Support all Shooting attacks in range, for example, or all Spirit rolls to recover from being Shaken. Inspire requires some sort of communi cation with those it affects.

edges.name: INVESTIGATOR
edges.text: Investigators spend a great deal of time researching ancient legends, working the streets, or deducing devilish mysteries. Whether it’s tracking down a rogue scientist, a fleshcrafter, or a ghost that leaves letters carved into corpses, Investigators are relentless. Investigators add +2 to Research rolls and Notice rolls made to search through desks for important papers, sift through stacks of junk mail for something of note, or spy obscured items from piles of junk or debris.

edges.name: IRON BOUND
edges.text: (Mad Scientist) Everyone has to learn their trade somewhere. Your mad scientist apprenticed to a master craftsman, or worked in a Hellstromme Industries factory, Smith & Robards workshop, or even one of the secret facilities belonging to the government. The alumni of these difficult and ground-breaking trials in the New Science are said to be “Iron Bound.” Your hero managed to leave his former employment with some of the equipment they worked on, and still have a few friends who can cut them a special deal when they’re in a pinch. The mad scientist starts with up to $2,000 in infernal devices or vehicles (see page 124), and reduces the listed price of any future devices purchased through that source by 25%. They might be able to get discounts through other outlets by reciting some of their bona fides and sharing experiences with other inventors (Marshal’s call).

edges.name: IRON JAW
edges.text: This bruider has a chin like a brick wall. The character adds +2 to Soak rolls and Vigor rolls to avoid Knockout Blows (see page 155).

edges.name: IRON WILL
edges.text: Willed The hero now adds their Strong Willed bonus to resist powers and negate their effects. Iron Will doesn’t stack with Brave, nor does it apply to subsequent rolls resulting from powers such as being Shaken by a damaging power, fear, or the like.

edges.name: JACK-OF-ALL-TRADES
edges.text: You meet all kinds out West—con men, tinkerers, ex-soldiers, and folks who’ve lived five lives before breakfast. The character makes a Smarts roll as an action after observing or studying some subject. They gain a d4 in the relevant skill with success, or d6 with a raise. They may try again after an hour of study, trial and effort, or immersion if they fail or want to try for a raise. This lasts until the character attempts to learn a different subject, whether they’re successful or not.

edges.name: KILLER INSTINCT
edges.text: This hero hates losing with a fiery passion, giving them a free reroll in any opposed Test they initiates.

edges.name: KNACK
edges.text: This Edge should only be taken during character creation, unless there’s a good reason for the hero to “discover” their latent powers at a later date. The Weird West is a superstitious place, where rumors and old wives’ tales abound. Occasionally, these folktales contain a germ of truth. A Knack is just that—folklore come true. Now you get to choose one of the special events that coincided with the time of your character’s birth. Bastard: Well, that’s what your hero is. Not the mean ornery kind, but the fatherless kind. A child born out of wedlock is said to be able to see the unseen. Spend a Benny to automatically be able to see invisible and hidden critters, or those that supernaturally blend in with their surroundings, for five rounds. Born on All Hallows’ Eve: They say those born on this day have a greater connection to the spirit world. They occasionally receive warnings if their actions are about to cause disastrous consequences. A hero who was Born on All Hallows’ Eve can spend Conviction to reroll a Critical Failure. Born on Christmas: A babe born on Christmas is particularly resistant to arcane effects powered by evil spirits. Only heroes with the Blessed or Shaman Arcane Background can take this Knack. If you wanted to take a different Arcane Background, this isn’t the Knack for you. When targeted by a power from any other Arcane Background, a hero with this Knack can spend a Benny to negate the effect and force the caster to make a Spirit roll (−4) or be Shaken. Breech Birth: A baby born butt-first is said to have the uncanny ability to heal injuries. Your hero is just such a person and can spend a Benny to use the healing power. They don’t need to roll and automatically gets a single success (thus healing one Wound). Seventh Son: Your hero is fated for greatness; his legend will loom large in the Weird West. This hombre has the ability to control fate. Any time a Benny is used in their presence, they can spend a Benny of their own to negate its effect. Shooting Star: A shooting star or comet lit up the sky at the time of your hero’s birth, and many believe it foretold their skills as a great leader. At the beginning of any combat, you may spend a Benny to double the character’s Command Range. This increased range lasts until the end of the encounter. Storm Born: Your character was born in the midst of a great storm and has little fear. When you spend a Benny to reroll a Fear check, you ignore all Fear penalties, both from the critter and the local Fear Level.

edges.name: LEVEL HEADED
edges.text: Fighters who can keep their cool when every one else is running for cover make deadly combatants. A hero with this Edge draws an additional Action Card in combat and chooses which to use.

edges.name: LEVEL HEADED (IMP)
edges.text: As above but the hero draws two additional cards and chooses which to keep.

edges.name: LIKE AN OAK
edges.text: Few things settle the nerves of a posse like the sight of a Ranger standing toe- to-toe with some horrific abomination. All allies within 12” of the Ranger negate up 2 points of Fear penalties when making a Fear check. If the Ranger fails their Fear check or is Shaken or Stunned, the allies do not get the benefit. If a group makes the check at the same time, the Ranger goes first.

edges.name: LIQUID COURAGE
edges.text: Some folks say whiskey makes a man brave. Others say it just makes ‘im stupid. But there’s a rare breed for whom a slug o’ moonshine lights a fire in the belly, chases off pain, and steels their hide—at least for a spell. Don’t expect ‘em to be sharp as a Bowie knife, though. This individual processes alcohol differently than most. The round after consuming a stiff drink (about eight ounces of hard liquor or equivalent), their Vigor increases one die type (increasing Toughness as well). The drinker can also ignore one level of Wound penalties (which stacks with other abilities that do the same). Smarts, Agility, and all linked skills suffer a −1 penalty for the duration, however. The effect lasts for one hour after it begins, at which point the boozer suffers a level of Fatigue for the next four hours.

edges.name: LUCK
edges.text: There’s no explainin’ it—this one’s just kissed by Lady Luck. When the cards fall, they fall right. When the bullet flies, it misses by an inch. You could call it destiny... or just one helluva lucky streak. They draw one extra Benny at the beginning of each game session, allowing them to succeed at important tasks more often than most, and survive incredible dangers.

edges.name: MAN OF A THOUSAND FACES
edges.text: This Edge helps Agents infiltrate their foes, given some supplies and the ability to study the enemy. The Agent adds +2 to their Performance rolls when trying to impersonate a general “type” of roughly similar build. There’s a −2 penalty for impersonating someone the target has heard of, a −4 for someone the target has seen before, or −6 for a specific individual or someone the target is familiar with. Use of this Edge requires clothing appropriate for the role. A disguise kit (see page 118) removes 2 points of penalties.

edges.name: MARKSMAN
edges.text: Shooting d8+ Stay still, aim true. The hero is a natural with ranged weapons. If they don’t move in a turn and fire no more than a Rate of Fire of 1 as their first action, they may add +1 to an Athletics (throwing) or Shooting roll, or ignore up to 2 points of penalties from Called Shots, Cover, Range, Scale, or Speed. This is a lesser version of the Aim maneuver and does not stack with it. Marksman doesn’t apply to additional attacks after the first.

edges.name: MARTIAL ARTIST
edges.text: The fighter has trained in basic martial arts. Their fists and feet are weapons (see Natural Weapons, page 159) so they’re always consid ered armed. They add +1 when striking with them and cause Strength+d4 damage. If they already have a Strength damage die from claws or the Brawler Edge, increase the damage a die type. Martial Artist does not add to damage from other Natural Weapons such as fangs or horns.

edges.name: MARTIAL WARRIOR
edges.text: Increase the warrior’s Fighting bonus to +2 and their damage die an additional step.

edges.name: MASTER
edges.text: in affected Trait The character’s Wild Die increases to a d10 when rolling the selected Expert Trait.

edges.name: MASTER OF ARMS
edges.text: Increase the hero’s Parry an additional +1 and their Fighting bonus damage die is now a d10.

edges.name: MASTER TACTICIAN
edges.text: The Tactician now gets a total of two extra Action Cards to distribute each round.

edges.name: MCGYVER
edges.text: A McGyver can improvise a device from common resources when the need arises. Given a few simple items, they can make a Repair roll to craft improvised weapons, explosives, or tools, that last until used or the end of the encounter (GM’s call). This takes one entire turn, and they can’t move or take any other actions while constructing the device. Failure means the device isn’t ready. A Critical Failure means they don’t have the right materials and can’t create the device this encounter. Success creates a minor explosive (2d4 explosive in a Small Blast Template), a one shot projectile weapon like a “zip gun” (Range 5/10/20, Damage 2d6), rickety raft, electrical source, etc. A raise creates a larger explosive (2d6 in a Medium Blast Template or 2d4 in a Large), a better ranged weapon (five shots, 2d8 damage, Range 10/20/40), a more stable raft, a more powerful battery, etc. The quality or power of the creation is completely up to the Game Master, but creativity should be rewarded, particularly in the most dire and dramatic situations.
edges.requirements: Novice, Smarts d6+, Notice d8+, Repair d6+

edges.name: MENACING
edges.text: Whether it’s the thousand-yard stare, that haunted look in their eyes, or the rumors of what they did back in Wichita, this one don’t need to talk much. They get +2 to Intimidation, and most folks know better than to poke the bear.
edges.requirements: Novice, any one of Bloodthirsty, Mean, Ruthless, or Ugly

edges.name: METAL MAGE
edges.text: Scientist), Occult d6+, Weird Science d8+ Metal mages use devices like any other weird scientist, but can also Deal with the Devil like a huckster (see page 85). Roll Occult instead of Gambling in step 3, and Weird Science instead of Spellcasting in step 5. Metal mages can’t take huckster Edges for more cards, but do get an extra card if they have at least 20 pounds of loose metal parts within arm’s reach, and another card if they burn an ounce of ghost rock in the process. It’s quite a spectacular show when a metal mage successfully Deals with the Devil! Metal bits swirl about the scientist, either appearing from thin air or levitating from whatever crates, bins, or toolkits are within a few feet of them. Unseen hands assemble the bits into a Hellish device or effect, twisting, shaping, turning and smashing pieces together in a storm of hot wind that smells of brimstone and madness. And if one looks closely, they just might see a demonic face howling with glee in the middle of the swirling metal maelstrom! There’s no denying something supernatural is happening when a metal mage deals with the Devil. Anyone who sees the event knows deviltry is afoot. Metal mages only resort to this measure as an absolute last resort when strangers are about. The devilish devices created in this way last as long as the power itself lasts, then collapse into a pile of their component parts—often burning hot or icy cold from the touch of the demonic forces that assembled them.  NEW AVAILABLE POWERS: Metal mages gain access to breakdown and mend, and may also take the huckster power trinkets. The device (Trapping) can be a clockwork assembler or some such, or it can just be a bag of random components the metal mage “assembles” when they activate the power. In any case, they always use their Weird Science skill.

edges.name: MIGHTY BLOW
edges.text: If your Action Card is a Joker, double the damage of your first successful Fighting attack this round.

edges.name: MIMIC
edges.text: Great supernatural power springs from the Hunting Grounds in one form or another. Sometimes a Harrowed attuned to that power can decipher it and wrestle it away for themself. When any power that uses the Spellcasting skill is used in sight of the Harrowed, they gain the ability to cast it themself. They may only do this once, and it must be within the same encounter they saw it used. The Harrowed uses Spellcasting to cast the spell if they have that skill, or Smarts if they don’t. Any Power Points or Modifiers must be identical. If a cultist casts a 3d6 bolt with AP 2 for four Power Points, the Harrowed may do exactly the same. A Critical Failure means the Harrowed is Fatigued and all currently maintained powers (if any) terminate.

edges.name: MR. FIX IT
edges.text: These tinkerers can patch up a steam wagon or a Gatling pistol while the parts are still smokin’. The mechanic adds +2 to Repair rolls. With a raise, they halve the time normally required to fix something. This means if a particular Repair job says a raise repairs it in half the time, a Mr. Fix It can finish the job in one-quarter the time with a raise.

edges.name: NATURAL LEADER
edges.text: This leader has proven themselves time and time again, gaining the respect of all those who fight by their side. Any Leadership Edge that says it applies only to Extras now applies to Wild Cards as well.

edges.name: NERVES OF STEEL
edges.text: Your hero has learned to fight on through the most intense pain. They may ignore 1 point of Wound penalties.

edges.name: NERVES OF STEEL (IMP)
edges.text: The hero ignores two points of Wound penalties.

edges.name: NEW POWERS
edges.text: (Any) Maybe they find an incantation in an old journal dug up from some long-dead ghost town, or hear a whisper in a dream from their old granny and wake up with an idea to call down holy fire on their foes. This Edge grants the character two new powers available to their Rank and Arcane Background. Or they can instead sacrifice one or both of those new powers to add a new Trapping to an existing power, adding an ice Trapping to their existing fire bolt, for example.

edges.name: NIGHTMARES
edges.text: One of the manitous’ duties in the spirit world is to torment dreamers. A Harrowed whose brain-worm gives them this power can share their misery, giving other living minds dark and terrible dreams. The Harrowed needs something from the target to inflict nightmares on her—it could be something of their body, like a hair, fingernail clipping, or blood stain; or it could be an item of some significance to them, such as a piece of jewelry, firearm, or even their trusty horse. The deader then simply decides if they want their manitou to torment the target each night. If so, they have the Night Terrors Hindrance for as long as the Harrowed wants to torment them. A victim can rid themself of the nightmares by killing the Harrowed or sleeping on sanctified ground. Dispel has no effect, but detect arcana senses an evil presence on the victim when they’re being tormented. With a raise, detect arcana also gives an impression of the Harrowed themself, perhaps a stench, a memory of when the item was taken, or their own dead eyes.

edges.name: NO MERCY
edges.text: When this killer spends a Benny to reroll damage, they add +2 to their final total.

edges.name: OLD HAND
edges.text: Heroic, Arcane Background (Huckster), Spellcasting d10+ With knowledge comes power, and this huckster knows when to say when. After you form a five-card poker hand when Dealing with the Devil, you can discard up to three cards and redraw!

edges.name: ORE EATER
edges.text: (Mad Scientist), Weird Science d6+ Though your mad scientist probably doesn’t want anyone to know it, they’ve developed a taste for ghost rock! Eating it raw isn’t really possible—it’s rock, after all—but it’s easy to powder or crush and sprinkle it into their favorite whiskey or spread it like salt over their vittles! This is obviously a dangerous practice, but greatly increases the Weird Scientist’s connection to the Hunting Grounds. They gains 5 Power Points when this Edge is taken (in addition to any gained from the Power Points Edge). The downside is that anytime they must roll on the Malfunction Table and rolls a 13, they get ghost rock fever instead of the Gremlin result! They can only contract the fever once, and must live or die by the rules set forth under Ghost Rock Fever, page 248.

edges.name: POSSESSION
edges.text: If a manitou’s good at anything, it’s taking control of someone else’s body. This power grants the Harrowed a limited ability to do the same. Controlling someone works exactly like the puppet power (page 190), but the Harrowed uses their Spirit −2 for the arcane skill roll (even if they have some other arcane skill). The deader is Distracted for as long as they maintain control. They may maintain the power as long as they want, but remain Distracted while doing so (they may not use Power Points even if they have them). If they’re Shaken, Stunned, or Wounded, they must make a Smarts roll or the power terminates as well.

edges.name: POWER POINTS
edges.text: (Any) Those who tap into eldritch energies always want more power. This Edge grants them an additional 5 Power Points. Power Points may be selected more than once, but only once per Rank. It may be taken as often as desired at Legendary Rank, but each grants only 2 additional points.

edges.name: POWER SURGE
edges.text: Background (Any), arcane skill d8+ The character recovers 10 Power Points when their Action Card is a Joker. This may not exceed their usual limit.

edges.name: PROFESSIONAL
edges.text: possible in affected Trait The character is an expert at a particular skill or attribute (their choice). This increases the Trait and its limit one step (a d12+1 becomes a d12+2, for example). This Edge may be selected once per Trait.

edges.name: PROVOKE
edges.text: A well-timed jab or insult can draw even the dead to anger. When this character lands a raise on a Taunt Test, they draw the enemy’s fire—protecting the rest of the posse from harm, while making themselves the target of their wrath. Once per turn, when your hero uses Taunt for a Test (page 164) and gets a raise, they may Provoke the foe. In addition to all the usual effects of the success and raise, the enemy suffers a −2 penalty to affect any other target besides the one who provoked them. This stacks with Distracted but not further instances of Provoke. Provoke lasts until a Joker is drawn, someone else Provokes the target, or the encounter ends. Provoke can affect multiple targets, and may be combined with Rabble Rouser (see below).

edges.name: QUICK
edges.text: Quick characters have lightning-fast reflexes and a cool head. Whenever you are dealt an Action Card of Five or lower, you may discard it and draw again until you get a card higher than Five, then choose which card to keep. Characters with both the Level Headed and Quick Edges first draw their additional card and choose which to take. If that card is a Five or less, the Quick Edge may be used to draw a replacement until it’s Six or higher, then choose which of those to keep.

edges.name: QUICK DRAW
edges.text: You draw two cards when spending a Benny for an additional Action Card at the beginning of a round. You may choose your final Action Card from any of your available choices, including additional draws from Level Headed, Quick, etc. You also add +2 to Athletics rolls made to interrupt others’ actions (including resisting being interrupted).

edges.name: RABBLE-ROUSER
edges.text: Whether stirring up a lynch mob, leading a miners’ revolt, or starting trouble in a saloon, this instigator can rile a whole crowd with just a few choice words. When they talk, tempers flare—and fists (or worse) tend to follow. As a limited action, a character with this Edge can make a social Test with Intimidation or Taunt against all enemies in a Medium Blast Template. The targets must be able to see and hear the hero clearly. Each defender resists and is affected by the Test separately.

edges.name: RALLY
edges.text: When things look grim, this leader can snap folks out of it like a slap across the face. Once per turn, they can make a Smarts roll at −2 as a free action. Success un-Shakes one ally in Command range; a raise un-Shakes all of ’em. Their rallying cry might be a barked order, a prayer, or a whistle that cuts through gunfire and fear alike.

edges.name: RANGER PROMOTION
edges.text: Your Ranger’s been promoted to Sergeant. They get a slight increase in pay, a Gatling shotgun or rifle if they like, and can request higher Favors. You can take this Edge a second time for a promotion to Lieutenant. This grants them Chapter 13 of Fugitives from Justice (see above) as well as a little extra dinero and the ability to request greater Favors. At Heroic Rank, a Ranger can take this Edge one last time to gain promotion to Captain, granting them access to 4-point Favors.

edges.name: RAPID FIRE
edges.text: The shooter is practiced at taking quick and accurate shots. As long as they’re armed with a fast-firing ranged weapon of some sort (such as a revolver or semi-automatic) and have enough ammunition to do so, they may increase their weapon’s Rate of Fire by 1 for any one of their Shooting attacks that turn.

edges.name: RAPID RECHARGE
edges.text: Background (Any) Power Points normally recharge at a rate of 5 points every hour spent resting (see Recharging, 169). This Edge increases that rate to 10 every hour.

edges.name: RELIABLE
edges.text: Dependable as the rising sun and twice as steady. This cowpoke’s the type you want by your side when the lead starts flyin’—they get a free reroll on Support rolls, and their word’s good as gold.

edges.name: REPUTATION
edges.text: Folks whisper stories when this one rides into town—heroic ballads or bloody legends, depending on how they live. With a good Reputation, they get a free reroll on Persuasion with anyone who’s heard their tale. With a bad one, they get +2 to Intimidation instead. Either way, people know.

edges.name: RETORT
edges.text: There’s nothing like throwing a fool’s insult right back in their face. When this character resists an Intimidation or Taunt Test with a raise, they leave their opponent Distracted.

edges.name: RICH
edges.text: Whether the individual was born with a silver spoon in their mouth or earned it through hard work, they’ve got more money than most. Rich heroes start with three times the normal starting funds for the setting ($750). If a regular income is appropriate for this setting, the hero receives a $5,000 annual salary.

edges.name: RIGHT HAND OF THE DEVIL
edges.text: Your hero is fast on the trigger and renowned far and wide as one mean hombre. Folks have taken to calling them the Right Hand of the Devil (or Left if your cowpoke is of the sinister rather than dexter persuasion). Whichever weapon your shootist typically uses in their favored hand has been infused with some of the mythic status they’re accorded, turning that weapon into a powerful relic. A relic weapon does an extra damage die of the same type as that weapon’s highest damage die. So a relic Winchester ‘76 would do a fearsome 3d8 damage. A hero usually dresses it up a bit with a silver filigree, pearl handles, and the like. It’s not a requirement, but most legends are partial to such decor. The Edge remains with the weapon, so if your shootist loses their gun, they lose the Edge as well—at least until they can get it back. And yes, anyone else who finds it in the meantime gets its benefits!
edges.requirements: Legendary, Trademark Weapon, Shooting, Fighting, or Athletics d10+

edges.name: RIGOR MORTIS
edges.text: A deader uses this power to inflict terrible pain on everyone who gets too close to their cadaverous corpse. Activating Rigor Mortis is a free action that creates a field of agony the size of a Medium Blast Template centered on the Harrowed. Everyone who enters the template (friend and foe alike) is wracked with pain and stiffness and Distracted. The condition terminates at the end of a victim’s turn if they’re no longer in the area of effect. Rigor Mortis can be maintained as long as the Harrowed desires, but terminates if they don’t make a Smarts roll when Shaken, Stunned, or Wounded.

edges.name: ROCK AND ROLL
edges.text: Experienced shooters learn to compensate for the recoil of those new-fangled Gatling weapons. If a character with Rock and Roll doesn’t move on their turn, they ignore the Recoil penalty when firing at a Rate of Fire of 2 or higher. (See Recoil, page 161.) Note: Of course “rock and roll” is an anachronism here in the Weird West, but we want to keep things kosher with our other settings, Marshal.

edges.name: ROLLER
edges.text: Your inveterate gambler draws two extra cards (total) when Dealing with the Devil.

edges.name: SCAVENGER
edges.text: Out in the dust and ruin, it’s not just bullets and brains that keep a cowpoke alive—it’s luck and the ability to find a horseshoe in a haystack. These folks always seem to lay hands on just the right gizmo, doohickey, or device when the need’s most dire. Once per encounter the hero may find, “suddenly remember,” or dig up some much- needed piece of equipment, a handful of ammunition, or some other useful device. The Game Master decides what constitutes an encounter, and has the final word on what can and can’t be found.

edges.name: SCHOLAR
edges.text: This ain’t your average snake-oil reader— this is a learned person, well-versed in dusty tomes, ancient languages, or maybe even forbidden lore. Pick any one of the following skills: Academics, Battle, Occult, Science, or a Smarts-based “knowledge”-type Trade, and add +2 to the total whenever they’re used. This Edge may be taken more than once if applied to different skills.

edges.name: SCOUT
edges.text: Scouts are masters of navigating the West’s vast wilderness. When the Marshal draws a face card while the posse is traveling— indicating an encounter—the Scout can make a Notice roll at −2 to detect the hazard, critter, or event first.
